title: Choose Kotoba's visual world (more Japanese)
question: A bolder hand weighted toward a Japanese feel, as you asked. Riso leads the deal; Ukiyo-e beat it on both axes.

options.label: Tokyo Riso Zine
options.lineage: Risograph zines from Tokyo print shops (Riso Kagaku is a Japanese machine)
options.thesis: Kotoba as a hand-printed Tokyo study zine: fluorescent inks, misregistered kana, grain you can feel.
options.viewport: A giant あ printed in fluoro pink over federal blue, slightly out of register, with a bold Vietnamese headline, a cut-paper 'Học thử ngay' button, and a spot-colour index rail (Hiragana · Katakana · Quiz).
options.risk: The paper-tone ground is close to the overused cream look; the inks have to own the page.
options.case: It's Japanese through print culture rather than clichés, but a zine says less about learning than a woodblock that builds up in layers.

raised.raise: Every quiz answer locks into place like a triggered trace: unanswered cards wobble out of register, answered ones snap into alignment.
The primary action gets its own framed moment on every screen; secondary actions recede.

options.label: Mokuhanga — Ukiyo-e Block Print
options.lineage: Edo woodblock prints, built one registered colour block at a time
options.thesis: Every kana starts as a black keyblock outline. Each time you get it right, another color block prints in, until the character is finished.
options.viewport: A deep indigo field with a large あ as a keyblock outline, filling with safflower red as a demo quiz is answered. A vertical title cartouche reads ことば, with red seals and a carved 'Học thử ngay' button.
options.risk: Ukiyo-e is the obvious Japan reference. It only works if the registration mechanic drives the product, not as wallpaper; indigo must own the page, not cream paper.
options.case: Wins both axes: unmistakably Japanese, and printing layers in is exactly what honest mastery progress looks like.

options.label: Tokyo Rain at Night
options.lineage: blue-hour to rainy-night city: neon kana signs doubled in wet streets
options.thesis: Learn to read the city: katakana and hiragana glowing on shop signs in the rain.
options.viewport: A rainy street of neon signs, each a real word (ラーメン, カラオケ), reflected below. Tapping a sign reads it out in Vietnamese.
options.case: Strong Japanese feel and aspirational for learners heading to Japan; the chart and quiz are harder to fit into a street scene.
options.risk: Cyberpunk-neon cliché, and it needs strong illustration assets.

options.label: Oscilloscope Bench
options.thesis: Pitch accent as a phosphor trace.
options.case: Loses both: not Japanese, too technical.
options.kept: Answered cards lock into place like a triggered trace.

options.label: Deco Cinema Lobby
options.case: Loses both: Western glamour, not Japan.

options.label: Moon-shadow Bazaar
options.kept: Each item keeps an origin ticket.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A friendly language-learning app landing page: mascot, green buttons, streaks.
canonCard.viewport: Centered headline, mascot illustration, and 'Bắt đầu' / 'Tôi đã có tài khoản' buttons.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every other language app.
